If you mean **minutes** ("how many minutes are there in one full day"):

There are **1,440 minutes** in one full day:
$$\text{24 hours} \times \text{60 minutes/hour} = \text{1,440 minutes}$$

---

If you mean **bytes** ("how many bytes are there in one full day"):
A day is a unit of time, not digital data, so it doesn't have an inherent byte size unless tied to a specific data rate:
* For example, at **1 byte per second**, one day (86,400 seconds) equals **86,400 bytes** (~86.4 KB).
